reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) directly demonstrates structural reversibility, sacrificial oxidation forming Pd@MOx shells, steric hindrance limiting Pd diffusion, and cuboctahedral-to-raft transformation for the exact CoNiCuZnPd/CeO2 system, accurately supporting all key premises of the hypothesis.
premises: Sub-nanometer CoNiCuZnPd HEA clusters on CeO2 nanorods exhibit structural reversibility under redox cycling.
Sacrificial oxidation of non-noble metals forms a protective oxide shell around Pd cores.
This oxide shell provides steric hindrance that limits Pd atom diffusion and sintering.
The reversible structural change involves a transformation from cuboctahedral to raft-like morphology.
These mechanisms preserve the single-phase solid solution and catalytic activity during NO reduction.
